FF158 implemented WebTransport.getStats() in https://bugzil.la/2007202

This adds return_object_property_* subfeatures for the members of the returned webTransportConnectionStats/WebTransportDatagramStats, based on the Firefox, WebKit and Deno source - thanks to Claude.
bytesSentOverhead is omitted since no engine returns it (Firefox: https://bugzil.la/2051624). Deno and Safari don't return anything useful, but they do expose the interfaces and mosty populate them with 0.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#45893

NOTE I am away on holiday and won't be back until late October. If you can make changes to make this PR mergable, please do, and merge it.

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds the missing compatibility data for the following menus.update() properties:

  • icons — Firefox 64
  • viewTypes — Firefox 64
  • visible — Firefox 63

Additional details

The compatibility data was added after investigating the Firefox WebExtensions implementation and documentation, Firefox release notes, and the related Mozilla Bugzilla issues.

The Firefox version information is based on the following sources:

  • menus.update.visible — Firefox 63, based on Firefox 63 release information and Bug 1482529.
  • menus.update.icons — Firefox 64, based on Firefox 64 release information and Bug 1414566.
  • menus.update.viewTypes — Firefox 64, based on Firefox 64 release information and Bug 1416839.

These properties were already part of the menus.update() API surface, but were not represented as individual compatibility subfeatures in BCD.

The three properties have therefore been added as separate subfeatures under webextensions.api.menus.update, following the existing BCD structure for WebExtensions API parameters and properties.

For browser support values outside Firefox, the entries follow the existing BCD compatibility data and mirroring conventions. In particular, safari_ios is represented as mirror for icons and viewTypes where the BCD linter confirms that the value can be automatically mirrored from Safari.

Related issues

Fixes #30615
items.title: fix(webextensions): add menus.update property compatibility data

Summary

Chrome 150 adds support for the focusgroup global attribute, the related focusgroupstart global attribute, and their reflected DOM properties. See https://chromestatus.com/feature/5637601087193088.

This PR adds support for the four features listed above. In particular, for the focusgroup attribute, I've added an individual datapoint for each of the attribute's tokens and behaviors. I have given the behaviors a prefix so they will all be kept together in the BCD table.

Notes:

  • The features are currently listed as non-standard because the spec PR is still open: whatwg/html#11723.
  • I am currently working on documenting only the v1 focusgroup features, which are all implemented. The v2 focusgroup features are currently experimental and subject to change, so I will handle them in a separate project in the future.
  • The WebIDL for the DOM properties is listed in the feature detection section of the explainer.

cc @janewman for technical input/questions. If you could check these to make sure I've not missed anything, that would be much appreciated. Thanks!

Test results and supporting details

Related issues

Add a note to the Firefox compatibility data for URLPattern documenting that lookahead and lookbehind assertions were not supported before Firefox 149.

The URLPattern API itself remains supported from Firefox 142; this change documents the historical limitation in its regular expression support rather than changing the API's version_added.

Additional details:

  • https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1998871
  • https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1984171

Bug 1998871 documents the URLPattern lookahead failure in Firefox 146 and records the fix in Firefox 149.

Google Chrome 152 removed internal implementation of Shared Storage API and turned all JS methods into stubs.

Related issues

Summary

Update html.elements.input.accept for iOS to mark support as partial.

iOS ignores filename extensions that it does not recognize, which can cause the file picker to accept only recognized extensions or no files when none are supported.

Additional Details:

The change keeps the existing audio/* limitation and adds the filename-extension limitation based on the reported iOS behavior and WebKit bug 279606.

Related issues

Fixes #26043

items.content_html:
Summary

Make the AccentColor and AccentColorText data more regular.

Test results and supporting details

  • Split up AccentColor and AccentColorText. This makes working with the notes much less confusing, since we have to cover just one behavior at a time.
  • Chrome desktop:
    • Shipped the values in version 149, not 150. Confirmed with a test case from Lea Verou — at least for the white/blue anti-fingeprinting behavior.
    • Revised the notes to focus on what the actual behavior is (using a fixed value). Why they did it is maybe something we could mention, but I don't think we typically do this for well-specified behavior.
  • Chrome Android:
    • I don't think either value shipped on Android. Lea's test case didn't work for me and it's corroborated by https://chromestatus.com/feature/5068127364186112.
  • Firefox: This seems to just work!
  • Safari: The original note is a mess (unclear plus spelling and punctuation issues). My own testing seemed to show that Safari just uses the black-on-blue values (changing the setting in the note text had no obvious behavior). Safari on iOS in BrowserStack didn't show anything special (black on blue).

Related issues

  • Initiated by web-platform-dx/web-features#4284
  • Previously: #21150
  • Previously: #30025
items.title: Clean up `AccentColor` and `AccentColorText` data
